 Print this Article 
 View Comments Jordan Walsh drew the assignment of defending Knicks guard Jalen Brunson Friday night. Barry Chin/Globe Staff The Celtics will be back in action Monday night when they take on the Bulls at TD Garden. They’ll be looking to make it two in a row following a 107-103 win over the Knicks in last Friday’s home opener . 
 Jayson Tatum bounced back from a rough performance in the season opener at Detroit to pour in 36 points and nine rebounds in the win. 
 Neemias Queta had 15 points, six rebounds and three blocked shots in 22 minutes off the bench in the win. 
 Related : Three big men frontcourt and center as part of Celtics’ bounceback win over the Knicks Jordan Walsh was in the starting lineup for both games, drawing the defensive assignment on Cade Cunningham against the Pistons, and Jalen Brunson against the Knicks. 
 “I thought he was special [against New York],” said Paul George. “He set the tone. Jalen is a handful, and for a young guy he can be a lot. Jordan took the challenge. He did a great job of navigating being physical and not being overly physical. He gave him some good looks defensively to frustrate him and get him out of rhythm.”

Enter Email Sign Up Caleb Wilson, the fourth pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, scored a game-high 30 points in Saturday’s game against the Wizards, and leads the Bulls averaging 22.3 points per game. 
 Here is a preview. 
 When: Monday, 7:30 p.m. 
 Where: TD Garden, Boston 
 TV: NBCSB. Radio: WBZ-FM 98.5. 
 Line: Boston -14. O/U: 232.5. 
 BULLS 
 Season record: 1-2. vs. spread: 1-2. Over/under: 1-1, 1 push 
 Last 10 games: 3-7. vs. spread: 4-6. Over/under: 3-6, 1 push 
 CELTICS 
 Season record: 1-1. vs. spread: 1-1. Over/under: 1-1 
 Last 10 games: 5-5. vs. spread: 4-6. Over/under: 3-7 
 TEAM STATISTICS 
 Points per game: Chicago 114.7, Boston 110.0 
 Points allowed per game: Chicago 128.0, Boston 112.0 
 Field goal percentage: Chicago .409, Boston .457 
 Opponent field goal percentage: Chicago .475, Boston .452 
 3-point percentage: Chicago .226, Boston .395 
 Opponent 3-point percentage: Chicago .355, Boston .388 
 Stat of the day: The Bulls are allowing 128.0 points per game. Only Milwaukee (129.0) has allowed more. 
 Notes: The Celtics have won nine of the last 11 meetings. … This is the first of two meetings between the teams this week. After tonight’s game, the Celtics will host the Nets on Tuesday before again welcoming the Bulls on Friday. The Bulls will be at the Knicks on Wednesday before coming coming back to Boston. … Only three games into the schedule, it has already been an up and down season for the Bulls, who lost to the Raptors by 43 points on opening night before answering with a seven-point victory over the Bucks. On Saturday, they dropped their home opener to the Wizards by four. … The Bulls have struggled from outside, averaging a league-worst 22.6 percent from beyond the arc. ”I want them to shoot the ball," Chicago coach Tiago Splitter said following Saturday’s 124-120 loss to Washington. “They can shoot. Part of their development is you are open, you got to shoot it. You practice every day; you have to take them in the game. Sometimes it’s the shot the other team is giving to you. It’s a team thing, not just one player. Everybody’s got to be better. We don’t have a 7-foot-3-inch guy that’s going to clean up the whole thing. So it’s got to be a team effort and awareness.”
